attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own Substack post, giving his view of X's planned news synthesis. It is not a quote of anyone else.

semantics.note: The firm 'will' is unhedged. Treating it as a causal claim about restricting synthesis to X posts fits the context. The baseline for 'even less' is implicit, and the drafter's comparison with LLMs in general is a reasonable reading.

contract.note: Reading 'less grounded' as lower factual accuracy than comparable synthesis without the source restriction is a fair, ordinary plain reading. Marcus named no measure or baseline, so the interpretation matters to the result.

evidence.note: Establishes the announced X-only design for news summaries, which is the claim's premise. It contains no accuracy comparison, so it is not evidence of the outcome.
Reports isolated fabricated Grok headlines. It has no matched baseline or error rate, so it cannot show that the restriction caused more errors.
A comparative accuracy study published before the cutoff, but it ran Grok with native web search, not X-only synthesis. It does not test the restriction.

reviews.rationale: The claim is firm and causal, and the contract is fair. But the packet has no controlled or comparable evaluation isolating the effect of confining synthesis to X posts. e1 shows only the design, e2 shows isolated errors, and e3 tests web-search configurations. A possibly relevant study (Prinetti, on SSRN) could not be opened. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.
